newsitem.title: CHINA: China says people to stay home for HK return party.
newsitem.headline: China says people to stay home for HK return party.

text.p: Beijing plans a huge party with 100,000 guests to mark the return of Hong Kong from British colonial rule at midnight on June 30 -- but most of the capital's residents are not invited, Chinese officials said on Monday.

Most Beijing residents should stay at home and watch on television the midnight extravaganza and a later mass rally at the capital's Workers' Stadium, said Long Xinmin of the city's organisation committee for the Hong Kong celebrations.
"The gathering and party on June 30 and the celebratory rally on July 1 are both events at which the participation of the masses is organised," Long told a news briefing in Beijing.
"We encourage the masses from other walks of life to stay at home and watch televison," he said.

Selected farmers, workers, intellectuals and officials would join a feast of songs, speeches, fireworks and dragon-dancing from 10.00 p.m. (1400 GMT) on June 30 to 5.10 a.m. on July 1 (2110 GMT on June 30), said fellow organiser Ji Lin.

The party in Beijing's central Tiananmen Square would centre around a 10-second countdown to the midnight moment when Hong Kong sovereignty would return to China after 156 years of rule from London, he said.
The transfer of sovereignty would be broadcast live from Hong Kong and would be followed by a mass rendition of the national anthem and rounds of fireworks, he said.

The controversial swearing-in of Hong Kong's post-colonial leadership -- which includes a China-backed provisional legislature that will replace the territory's current elected body -- would also be broadcast live to Tiananmen Square.
Britain and the United States will boycott the swearing-in, although other Western nations that have also condemned the scrapping of the current legislature are set to attend.
The Tiananmen Square party, to be paid for out of central and city government funds, would end with the ceremonial dawn raising of the Chinese flag, Ji said.

The overnight party would be followed on the evening of July 1 by a rally in Beijing's Workers's Stadium, where a cast of 18,000 would dance in celebration at the end of more than a century of colonial humiliation, said organiser Zhu Zubu.
"It will be grander than any event we have held in the stadium before," Zhu said.
State television showed performers practising in the empty stadium, with thousands holding coloured boards to represent a huge flag with Hong Kong's new bauhinia flower symbol.
Separate parts of the performance would display the different emotions surrounding Hong Kong's return to China, Zhu said.

"The part called 'Affections Throughout the Country' is designed to reflect the great affection with which the Chinese people await Hong Kong's return and their great joy at being able to remove the stains of the past 100 years," he said.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin, who will be in Hong Kong for the formal handover, is expected to make a speech to the rally.
